questions.stem: A motor transfers 6000 J of energy in 30 seconds. What is its power output?
questions.explanation: Power = energy transferred / time = 6000 / 30 = 200 W. Option A multiplies instead of dividing. Option C divides the wrong way round. Option D adds the values. Power is the rate of energy transfer, measured in watts (W).

questions.stem: Two students each carry identical 50 N boxes up the same flight of stairs. Student A takes 10 seconds and Student B takes 20 seconds. Which statement is correct?

options.text: Student A does more work and has more power
Both do the same work, but Student A has double the power
Student B does more work because they take longer
Both have the same power because they carry the same weight

questions.explanation: Both students carry the same weight through the same height, so they do the same work (W = F x d). However, Student A does this work in half the time, so their power is double (P = W/t). Power depends on how quickly work is done, not just how much work is done.

questions.stem: A 500 W microwave oven runs for 2 minutes. How much energy does it transfer?
questions.explanation: Energy = power x time. Time must be in seconds: 2 minutes = 120 s. Energy = 500 x 120 = 60 000 J. Option A uses 2 instead of 120 (forgetting to convert minutes to seconds). Always convert time to seconds when using watts.

questions.stem: A crane lifts a 400 kg load 10 m in 8 seconds. What is the useful power output of the crane? (g = 10 m/s^2)
questions.explanation: Work done = mgh = 400 x 10 x 10 = 40 000 J. Power = work / time = 40 000 / 8 = 5 000 W (5 kW). Option A divides by 80 instead of 8. Option C incorrectly calculates the work. Option D gives the work done, not the power.

questions.stem: A 60 W light bulb and a 10 W LED bulb both produce the same amount of light. What can be concluded?

options.text: The light bulb is more efficient because it uses more power
The LED bulb is more efficient because it wastes less energy as heat
Both are equally efficient since they produce the same light
The LED bulb is more powerful

questions.explanation: The LED produces the same useful light output using only 10 W compared to 60 W for the filament bulb. This means the LED converts a higher proportion of its input energy into light (useful output), wasting less as heat. The filament bulb wastes most of its 60 W as thermal energy. Using more power does not mean more efficient; it means more energy is consumed per second.
